title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Averages
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: Onion is sold for 5 consecutive months at the rate of Rs 10, 20, 25, 25, and 50 per kg, respectively. A family spends a fixed amount of money on onion for each of the first three months, and then spends half that amount on onion for each of the next two months. The average expense for onion, in rupees per kg, for the family over these 5 months is closest to
questions.explain:
Let the fixed amount spent in each of the first three months be ₹ $E$. The amount spent in months 4 and 5 is ₹ $E/2$.
Total money spent over 5 months = $E + E + E + E/2 + E/2 = 4E$.
Total quantity bought:
Month 1: $E/10$ kg
Month 2: $E/20$ kg
Month 3: $E/25$ kg
Month 4: $(E/2)/25 = E/50$ kg
Month 5: $(E/2)/50 = E/100$ kg
Total quantity = $E \left(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{50} + \frac{1}{100}\right)$.
Taking LCM of 100: Total quantity = $E \left(\frac{10 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 1}{100}\right) = \frac{22E}{100} = 0.22E$ kg.
Average expense (Rs per kg) = $\frac{\text{Total money spent}}{\text{Total quantity bought}} = \frac{4E}{0.22E} = \frac{400}{22} = 18.18$.
Closest to 18.
